newsitem.title: CHINA: Nearly 25 percent of Chinese know little of AIDS.
newsitem.headline: Nearly 25 percent of Chinese know little of AIDS.

text.p: Nearly one quarter of China's people lack even basic knowledge about AIDS while two percent have never heard of the disease, the Beijing Youth Daily said on Wednesday.

A survey by the outspoken Southern Weekend newspaper of 1,000 households in four cities showed that 24 percent of respondents knew little or nothing about AIDS while just five percent said they were very familiar with the disease, the daily said.
About 69 percent said they had some understanding of AIDS and two percent said they had never heard of the disease, it quoted the survey as saying said.

Differences in understanding of AIDS were especially marked along educational lines, with educated people more likely to read newspapers that were the main source of AIDS information in China, it said.
Younger people were more likely to know more about the disease than older people, it said.

Most of those who said they knew something about the disease had identified sexual activity and blood exchange as the main means of transmission but 16 percent believed it could be spread through casual contact, it said.
About one-third of respondents said they thought AIDS (Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome) was a major problem in China, it said.
At the end of October China reported a total of 5,157 cases of people infected with HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) that causes AIDS and 133 patients with full-blown AIDS.
Officials say the actual number of those infected could be as high as 100,000. The population of China is about 1.2 billion.
